observations: Photo shows a PlayStation console with a DualShock-style controller in front.
Console appears to be the older/large “fat” PS4 design (not the slim).
There are visible scuffs/smudges on the console front panel and controller surfaces.
No clear view of model/serial label, ports, or any power/boot screen.

read_from: photo 0 (console shape and controller style indicate PS4 fat)

claims.claim: PS4 Fat Double Pad Good Condition
claims.evidence: Only one controller is clearly visible in photo 0; console condition is not verifiable (no boot/test, no close-ups of ports/drive).

risks.risk: Seller may not include the second controller (“double pad”).
risks.proof: Photo showing both controllers side-by-side (front + back) and/or a video of both controllers being packed.
risks.if_unproven: Price as PS4 fat with 1 controller only.

risks.risk: Console may have faults (won’t power on, overheating, disc drive issues, HDMI/ports problems). Photos can’t confirm functionality.
risks.proof: Short video: power on + home screen + audio/video working; show disc tray opening/closing if applicable.
risks.if_unproven: Price as not tested / worst-case not fully working.

risks.risk: Storage size and whether it’s HDD/SSD is unknown; affects value.
risks.proof: Photo of system storage screen (Settings > Storage) or a screenshot/video showing storage capacity.
risks.if_unproven: Price as standard HDD with unknown capacity.

risks.risk: Region/account status and whether it’s reset/ready for use is unknown.
risks.proof: Photo/video of the initial setup screen or Settings > Users showing it’s signed out and reset.
risks.if_unproven: Price as account/activation status unknown (assume extra hassle).

proof_requests: Show both controllers clearly (front and back) to confirm “double pad”.
Video proof of power-on to the PS4 home screen (and audio/video).
Photo/video of Settings > Storage (capacity and HDD/SSD).
Photo/video of the console ports (HDMI, USB) and a close-up of the model/serial label.
response.reason: The photos confirm a PS4 fat look, but key value drivers can’t be verified remotely: whether there are two controllers and whether the console actually works (no boot/test). Without that, a safe worst-case price can’t be set confidently.
